_meta.title: Shirk
_meta.description: Associating partners with Allah: its types, its dangers and how to avoid it.

shirk-easy-1.question: What is the Arabic term for associating partners with Allah?
shirk-easy-1.explanation: Shirk means ascribing a partner or rival to Allah in His Lordship, worship, or Names and Attributes.

shirk-easy-2.question: What is the greatest sin in Islam?
shirk-easy-2.explanation: Allah does not forgive shirk if one dies upon it without repentance, while He may forgive other sins.

shirk-easy-3.question: Does Allah forgive major shirk if a person dies without repenting from it?
options: No, He does not forgive it
Only if the person was a scholar
Only on the Day of Judgment
shirk-easy-3.explanation: Allah explicitly states that He does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but may forgive anything less than that for whom He wills.

shirk-easy-4.question: What is the opposite of Tawhid?
shirk-easy-4.explanation: Tawhid is the pure Oneness of Allah; shirk is its direct opposite — associating partners with Him.

shirk-easy-5.question: How many main types of shirk do scholars commonly divide it into?
shirk-easy-5.explanation: Scholars primarily divide shirk into major shirk (shirk akbar) which expels from Islam, and minor shirk (shirk asghar) which does not.

shirk-easy-6.question: What is major shirk (shirk akbar)?
options: Associating partners with Allah in a way that takes one out of Islam
shirk-easy-6.explanation: Major shirk includes worshipping others besides Allah, calling upon the dead, or believing someone shares in Allah's unique rights.

shirk-easy-7.question: What is minor shirk (shirk asghar)?
options: Actions described as shirk in the texts that do not expel from Islam, such as showing off
shirk-easy-7.explanation: Minor shirk includes riya (showing off), swearing by other than Allah, and certain superstitious practices; it diminishes Tawhid but does not remove one from Islam.

shirk-easy-8.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ say he feared for his ummah more than the Dajjal?
shirk-easy-8.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said he feared for his ummah the hidden shirk more than the Dajjal, referring to showing off in worship.

shirk-easy-9.question: What is riya?
options: Showing off in acts of worship to gain praise from people
shirk-easy-9.explanation: Riya is performing deeds of worship so that people will see and praise them, rather than purely for Allah; it is a form of minor/hidden shirk.

shirk-easy-10.question: Is swearing by other than Allah permitted?
options: No, it is a form of shirk
shirk-easy-10.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed shirk.' It is generally classified as minor shirk.

shirk-easy-11.question: What should a Muslim say instead of 'What Allah wills and so-and-so wills'?
options: What Allah wills and so-and-so wills (same)
What Allah alone wills, then what so-and-so wills
shirk-easy-11.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ corrected the phrase that equates others with Allah and taught to say 'What Allah wills, then what so-and-so wills.'

shirk-easy-12.question: What is the fate of one who dies upon major shirk without repentance?
options: He will enter Paradise after purification
Paradise is forbidden for him and the Fire is his abode
shirk-easy-12.explanation: Allah says that whoever associates partners with Him, Paradise is forbidden for him and his abode is the Fire.

shirk-easy-13.question: Does merely uttering 'La ilaha illallah' protect from shirk if one still worships others?
options: Yes, the words alone are enough
No, the conditions of the Shahadah must be fulfilled, including sincerity and rejecting other deities
shirk-easy-13.explanation: The Shahadah requires knowledge, certainty, sincerity, truthfulness, love, submission, acceptance, and rejection of all that is worshipped besides Allah.

shirk-easy-14.question: What is an example of major shirk in worship (Uluhiyyah)?
options: Calling upon a deceased saint for help
shirk-easy-14.explanation: Directing dua, seeking help, or any act of worship to anyone other than Allah is major shirk.

shirk-easy-15.question: What is an example of shirk in Lordship (Rububiyyah)?
options: Believing Allah is the only Creator
Believing that someone else creates, gives life, or controls the universe along with Allah
shirk-easy-15.explanation: Shirk in Rububiyyah is ascribing to others the actions that belong only to Allah: creating, sustaining, giving life and death, and controlling the universe.

shirk-easy-16.question: What is an example of shirk in Names and Attributes?
options: Calling Allah by His revealed Names
Giving Allah's unique Names or Attributes to created beings, or likening Allah to His creation
shirk-easy-16.explanation: Shirk in Asma wa Sifat includes naming idols after Allah's Names or believing that any creature shares Allah's unique perfect Attributes.

shirk-easy-17.question: Are amulets (tamimah) that are believed to protect from harm permissible?
options: No, wearing them for protection is a form of shirk
shirk-easy-17.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever wears an amulet has committed shirk.' Seeking protection through means not legislated by Allah is shirk.

shirk-easy-18.question: What did Luqman advise his son regarding shirk?
options: Do not associate partners with Allah; indeed, shirk is a great injustice
shirk-easy-18.explanation: Luqman said to his son: 'O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is a great injustice.'

shirk-easy-19.question: Is it permissible to slaughter an animal for a grave or a jinn?
options: Yes, if done with good intention
Only if the meat is given in charity
shirk-easy-19.explanation: Slaughtering for other than Allah is an act of worship directed to other than Him and is major shirk.

shirk-easy-20.question: What is the first of the ten nullifiers of Islam mentioned by scholars?
options: Shirk in the worship of Allah
shirk-easy-20.explanation: The first nullifier is shirk in worshipping Allah, such as slaughtering for other than Him or calling upon others.

shirk-easy-21.question: Does major shirk nullify all previous good deeds?
options: Yes, if one dies upon it without repentance, previous deeds are nullified
Only if the person was a hypocrite
shirk-easy-21.explanation: Allah says that if they had associated others with Him, all that they used to do would have become worthless.

shirk-easy-22.question: What is the correct response when someone says 'By the life of so-and-so'?
options: Remind that one should swear only by Allah
shirk-easy-22.explanation: Swearing by other than Allah is prohibited and is a form of minor shirk; one should swear only by Allah or remain silent.

shirk-easy-23.question: Is believing that the stars control events in the universe a form of shirk?
options: Yes, if one believes the stars themselves cause events, it is major shirk
shirk-easy-23.explanation: Believing that stars or planets control destiny or cause rain and events is shirk in Rububiyyah.

shirk-easy-24.question: What is the meaning of 'La ilaha illallah' in relation to shirk?
options: There is no creator except Allah
There is no god truly worthy of worship except Allah (negating all false objects of worship)
shirk-easy-24.explanation: The Kalima negates all that is worshipped besides Allah and affirms that only Allah deserves worship, thereby rejecting shirk.

shirk-easy-25.question: Can a person who commits major shirk still be considered a Muslim?
options: No, major shirk expels a person from Islam
shirk-easy-25.explanation: Major shirk takes a person out of the fold of Islam; repentance is required to return to Islam.

shirk-easy-26.question: What is hidden shirk (shirk khafi) often referring to?
options: Subtle forms such as riya (showing off) that people may not notice
Only the shirk of the past nations
shirk-easy-26.explanation: Hidden shirk is more inconspicuous than the crawling of a black ant on a black rock in the dark night; it includes beautifying prayer because others are watching.

shirk-easy-27.question: Is it shirk to say 'If not for Allah and so-and-so, this would not have happened'?
options: Yes, it is a form of minor shirk because it equates others with Allah
Only if the person is a non-Muslim
shirk-easy-27.explanation: Equating others with Allah in will or causation by using 'and' is a form of minor shirk; one should say 'If not for Allah, then so-and-so.'

shirk-easy-28.question: What is the ruling on seeking help from the dead at graves?
options: It is permissible if the person was a wali
shirk-easy-28.explanation: Calling upon the dead for help, relief, or intercession in matters only Allah can do is major shirk.

shirk-easy-29.question: Does ignorance completely excuse major shirk in all cases?
options: Not necessarily; the basic message of Tawhid is clear, and one must learn
shirk-easy-29.explanation: While Allah is Just, the fundamental call of all Prophets was Tawhid, and adults are responsible to seek knowledge of what is required of them.

shirk-easy-30.question: What is the reward for one who avoids shirk and dies upon pure Tawhid?
shirk-easy-30.explanation: The one who dies free of major shirk will eventually enter Paradise, even if after purification if he had major sins.

shirk-easy-31.question: Is fortune-telling or believing in fortune-tellers a form of shirk?
options: Yes, claiming knowledge of the unseen or believing those who claim it is shirk
shirk-easy-31.explanation: Knowledge of the unseen belongs only to Allah; claiming it or believing those who claim it is a form of shirk.

shirk-easy-32.question: What should a Muslim do if they realize they have fallen into a form of shirk?
options: Immediately repent sincerely to Allah, abandon the act, and return to pure Tawhid
shirk-easy-32.explanation: Repentance from shirk is accepted if done sincerely before death; one must abandon the shirk and renew pure Tawhid.

shirk-easy-33.question: Is loving someone more than Allah a form of shirk?
options: If the love leads to preferring that person over obedience to Allah, it can be a form of shirk
Only if the person is a non-Muslim
Love has no relation to shirk
shirk-easy-33.explanation: Allah criticizes those who take rivals and love them as they love Allah; true love for Allah requires preferring His commands.

shirk-easy-34.question: What is the ruling on hanging blue beads or 'evil eye' charms for protection?
options: It is a form of minor shirk if done for protection, as it is an unlegislated means
Only for decoration it is fine
shirk-easy-34.explanation: Using objects as protection when Allah has not made them a means is a form of minor shirk.

shirk-easy-35.question: Did the polytheists of Makkah believe in Allah as Creator?
options: Yes, many affirmed Allah as Creator but committed shirk in worship
shirk-easy-35.explanation: The mushrikin of Makkah largely affirmed Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah but committed shirk in Uluhiyyah by directing worship to others.

shirk-easy-36.question: What is the safest way to protect oneself from shirk?
options: Learn pure Tawhid, make dua for steadfastness, and avoid all forms of associating partners with Allah
shirk-easy-36.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught dua seeking refuge from associating partners with Allah knowingly or unknowingly.

shirk-intermediate-1.question: What are the three main categories of shirk corresponding to the three categories of Tawhid?
options: Shirk in belief, speech, and action
Shirk in Rububiyyah, Uluhiyyah, and Asma wa Sifat
shirk-intermediate-1.explanation: Just as Tawhid has three categories, shirk opposes each: associating partners in Lordship, in worship, and in Names and Attributes.

shirk-intermediate-2.question: What is the difference between major and minor shirk regarding one's status as a Muslim?
options: Major shirk expels from Islam; minor shirk does not but is still a major sin
shirk-intermediate-2.explanation: Major shirk nullifies Islam and, if one dies upon it, leads to eternal Fire. Minor shirk diminishes perfect Tawhid but leaves one within Islam.

shirk-intermediate-3.question: When does swearing by other than Allah become major shirk?
options: When the person believes the one sworn by has the same status or veneration as Allah
Only if said in a mosque
shirk-intermediate-3.explanation: Swearing by other than Allah is normally minor shirk; it becomes major if the heart holds the object of the oath equal to Allah in glorification.

shirk-intermediate-4.question: What is the ruling on saying 'What Allah wills and you will' to a person?
options: It is a form of minor shirk; one should say 'What Allah alone wills'
Only permissible for the Prophet ﷺ
shirk-intermediate-4.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ corrected a man who said this to him, saying: 'Have you made me a rival to Allah? Say: What Allah alone wills.'

shirk-intermediate-5.question: Is wearing an amulet containing Quranic verses free from any concern?
options: Many scholars still regard it as disliked or a form of minor shirk because it is an unlegislated means; verbal ruqyah is safer
shirk-intermediate-5.explanation: Even Quranic amulets are disputed; the safest path is to recite ruqyah and dua verbally as the Prophet ﷺ taught, without hanging objects.

shirk-intermediate-6.question: What is the ruling on going to a fortune-teller or soothsayer and believing them?
options: Disbelief (kufr) if one believes they know the unseen
shirk-intermediate-6.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever goes to a soothsayer and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ.

shirk-intermediate-7.question: What is shirk in obedience (related to legislation)?
options: Making lawful what Allah made unlawful or unlawful what Allah made lawful, and following that as religion
shirk-intermediate-7.explanation: Taking rabbis, monks, or anyone else as legislators who make the lawful unlawful and vice versa is a form of major shirk, as in Surah At-Tawbah 9:31.

shirk-intermediate-8.question: What is the correct belief about intercession (shafa'ah) to avoid shirk?
options: Intercession is only by Allah's permission and for those with whom He is pleased
shirk-intermediate-8.explanation: All intercession belongs to Allah; no one intercedes except after His permission. Seeking intercession by calling upon the dead is shirk.

shirk-intermediate-9.question: What is the difference between permissible tawassul and forbidden istighathah?
options: Permissible tawassul is through one's deeds, Allah's Names, or the living; forbidden istighathah is calling upon the dead for help
Only tawassul through the Prophet ﷺ after his death by calling him is allowed
shirk-intermediate-9.explanation: Asking Allah by His Names or one's good deeds is permitted. Calling upon the deceased for help is major shirk.

shirk-intermediate-10.question: Is it major shirk to believe that a wali (saint) can independently benefit or harm?
options: Yes, because benefit and harm belong only to Allah
It is recommended in some cultures
shirk-intermediate-10.explanation: Believing any created being has independent power to benefit or harm is shirk in Rububiyyah.

shirk-intermediate-11.question: What is the ruling on magic (sihr) that involves seeking help from jinn or other than Allah?
options: It is major kufr and shirk
shirk-intermediate-11.explanation: Magic that involves invoking other than Allah or believing in its independent power is major disbelief and shirk.

shirk-intermediate-12.question: What is the correct understanding of the hadith 'Whoever dies while knowing there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise'?
options: Mere utterance is enough regardless of actions
It refers to one who dies upon pure Tawhid free of major shirk
It means no deeds are required
It applies only to the Companions
shirk-intermediate-12.explanation: The hadith affirms that the one who dies upon Tawhid (free of major shirk) will enter Paradise, though major sinners may first be purified if Allah wills.

shirk-intermediate-13.question: What is the danger of excessive praise of the righteous that can lead to shirk?
options: It can lead to elevating them to the level of worship, as happened with previous nations
shirk-intermediate-13.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ warned against excessive praise, and previous nations fell into shirk by exaggerating the status of the righteous and taking their graves as places of worship.

shirk-intermediate-14.question: Is it permissible to make a vow (nadhr) to other than Allah?
options: No, a vow is an act of worship and must be made only to Allah
Only if the vow is for charity
shirk-intermediate-14.explanation: Making a vow to a grave, saint, or anyone other than Allah is major shirk because vows are a form of worship.

shirk-intermediate-15.question: What is the ruling on taking the graves of the righteous as places of worship?
options: It is forbidden and a means to shirk; the Prophet ﷺ cursed those who did so
Only for Prophets it is allowed
shirk-intermediate-15.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ cursed the Jews and Christians for taking the graves of their Prophets as places of worship and forbade this for his ummah.

shirk-intermediate-16.question: What is the status of one who does not regard the mushrikin as disbelievers?
options: He is still a complete Muslim
He himself commits an act of disbelief according to scholarly consensus
It is only a difference of opinion
shirk-intermediate-16.explanation: One of the nullifiers of Islam is not declaring the polytheists as disbelievers, or doubting their disbelief, or approving their way.

shirk-intermediate-17.question: What is the correct way to seek protection from the evil eye and envy?
options: Use the authentic ruqyah and dua from the Quran and Sunnah, and put one's trust in Allah
shirk-intermediate-17.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught specific dua and ruqyah for protection; relying on unlegislated means is a form of shirk.

shirk-intermediate-18.question: Is it shirk to believe that the Prophet ﷺ has knowledge of the unseen independently?
options: Yes, knowledge of the unseen belongs only to Allah; the Prophet ﷺ knew only what Allah revealed to him
It is a high level of faith
shirk-intermediate-18.explanation: Allah says that none in the heavens or earth knows the unseen except Him. The Prophet ﷺ was given specific knowledge by revelation, not independent knowledge of the ghayb.

shirk-intermediate-19.question: What is the ruling on showing off (riya) in a portion of one's deed?
options: The entire deed is still accepted
The portion done for show is nullified; if the original intention was for Allah, the rest may remain
shirk-intermediate-19.explanation: If a person begins a deed for Allah then is affected by riya, the portion affected is compromised; pure sincerity is required for full acceptance.

shirk-intermediate-20.question: What is the danger of saying 'In the name of Allah and the name of the shaykh' when starting something?
options: It is a form of minor shirk because it associates others with Allah in beginning actions
shirk-intermediate-20.explanation: Beginning actions with the name of other than Allah, or equating others with Him, is a form of shirk in speech.

shirk-intermediate-21.question: Is it permissible to ask a living righteous person to make dua for you?
options: Yes, this is permissible tawassul through the living
Only if the person is a scholar
shirk-intermediate-21.explanation: Requesting dua from a living person is allowed and was practiced by the Companions; it is not the same as calling upon the dead.

shirk-intermediate-22.question: What is the ruling on believing that the universe is eternal and not created by Allah?
options: It is major shirk (or kufr) because it denies Allah as the Creator
shirk-intermediate-22.explanation: Denying that Allah created the universe and affirming its eternity is a form of shirk by negation in Rububiyyah.

shirk-intermediate-23.question: What is the correct response to someone who claims that calling upon the Prophet ﷺ after his death is not shirk?
options: Explain that calling upon the dead is major shirk, and the Prophet ﷺ taught us to call upon Allah alone
shirk-intermediate-23.explanation: The Quran and Sunnah consistently direct all dua to Allah alone. The dead cannot hear or respond in the manner of the living.

shirk-intermediate-24.question: What is the ruling on using 'lucky' charms or objects believed to bring good fortune?
options: It is a form of minor shirk because one is attaching to a means that has no basis in the Shariah
shirk-intermediate-24.explanation: Attaching the heart to unlegislated means for benefit or protection is a form of minor shirk.

shirk-intermediate-25.question: What is the status of one who prefers the judgment of taghut (false laws) over the judgment of Allah?
options: He is a sinner but Muslim
He has committed an act of disbelief
shirk-intermediate-25.explanation: Preferring other laws over the Shariah of Allah, or believing they are better, is one of the nullifiers of Islam.

shirk-intermediate-26.question: Is it shirk to fear other than Allah in the sense of the fear of worship?
options: Yes, the fear that includes reverence and submission due only to Allah, if directed to others, is a form of shirk
Only if the person is a non-Muslim
Fear has no relation to shirk
shirk-intermediate-26.explanation: Natural fear is not shirk, but the fear of worship (khawf al-ibadah) that includes reverence and hope is due only to Allah.

shirk-intermediate-27.question: What is the ruling on sacrificing an animal at a particular place believing the place itself has special power?
options: If one believes the place has independent power, it is shirk; sacrifice must be for Allah alone
Permissible if the meat is distributed
shirk-intermediate-27.explanation: Sacrifice is an act of worship that must be purely for Allah; attributing power to places or objects is shirk.

shirk-intermediate-28.question: What is the correct understanding of the statement 'The shirk of this ummah is more hidden than the crawling of an ant'?
options: Subtle forms of shirk, especially riya and attachment of the heart, can be very hidden and require constant vigilance
It refers only to the past
shirk-intermediate-28.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ warned that shirk in this ummah is more hidden than a black ant on a black rock in the darkness of night.

shirk-intermediate-29.question: Is it permissible to seek blessing (tabarruk) from the remnants of the Prophet ﷺ that are authentically established?
options: The Companions sought blessing from things that touched him during his life; after his death, the focus is on following his Sunnah
Yes, from any claimed relic today without verification
shirk-intermediate-29.explanation: Tabarruk with the Prophet's physical remnants was practiced by the Companions while he was alive. After his death, the correct path is adherence to his teachings, not seeking unverified relics.

shirk-intermediate-30.question: What is the ruling on believing that some people know what is in the hearts of others without revelation?
options: It is a form of shirk or false claim because knowledge of the hearts belongs to Allah
It is common among the righteous
shirk-intermediate-30.explanation: Allah alone knows what is in the hearts. Claiming such knowledge without revelation is a false claim that can involve shirk in Attributes.

shirk-intermediate-31.question: What should a person do if they have been involved in minor shirk such as riya?
options: Ignore it because it is minor
Repent, renew sincerity, and strive to make all deeds purely for Allah
Only perform deeds in secret forever
shirk-intermediate-31.explanation: Minor shirk requires repentance and correction of intention. The Prophet ﷺ taught to seek refuge from associating partners with Allah even unknowingly.

shirk-intermediate-32.question: Is it shirk to obey a created being in disobedience to Allah?
options: If one obeys a created being in clear disobedience to Allah while believing it is correct, it can reach the level of shirk
Only if the person is a ruler
Obedience has no relation to shirk
shirk-intermediate-32.explanation: Absolute obedience is due only to Allah. Obeying others in what is disobedience to Allah, while regarding it as correct, is a form of taking them as lords.

shirk-intermediate-33.question: What is the ruling on astrology and believing that the position of stars determines one's destiny?
options: It is a form of shirk because it attributes control of events to the stars
shirk-intermediate-33.explanation: Believing that stars determine destiny or events is shirk in Rububiyyah. Studying stars for navigation or time is different.

shirk-intermediate-34.question: What is the correct belief about the power of dua?
options: Dua is a means; Allah alone answers and has full power
Only the dua of saints is answered
Dua is unnecessary because of Qadr
shirk-intermediate-34.explanation: Dua is one of the greatest acts of worship and a means that Allah has legislated; the response is entirely in Allah's hands.

shirk-intermediate-35.question: What is the danger of the statement 'The shaykh will take care of my affairs in the grave and on the Day of Judgment'?
options: No danger if said with love
It is major shirk because it attributes to a created being what belongs only to Allah
shirk-intermediate-35.explanation: Believing that any created being controls one's fate in the grave or on the Day of Judgment is major shirk in Rububiyyah and Uluhiyyah.

shirk-intermediate-36.question: What is the ruling on believing that some natural objects (trees, stones, etc.) have independent power to benefit or harm?
options: It is major shirk because benefit and harm belong only to Allah
It is permissible if done for barakah
shirk-intermediate-36.explanation: Attributing independent power of benefit or harm to any created object is major shirk in Rububiyyah.

shirk-advanced-1.question: What is the precise definition of major shirk according to the scholars of Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: Ascribing to other than Allah something that belongs exclusively to Allah in Rububiyyah, Uluhiyyah, or Asma wa Sifat, in a way that expels from Islam
shirk-advanced-1.explanation: Major shirk is to give to others the rights that are unique to Allah, whether in His Lordship, His exclusive right to be worshipped, or His Names and Attributes.

shirk-advanced-2.question: What is the difference between shirk in belief (i'tiqad) and shirk in action?
options: Shirk in belief is holding a creed that associates partners with Allah; shirk in action is performing acts of worship for other than Allah
shirk-advanced-2.explanation: Both can be major. Belief that someone shares in Allah's unique attributes is shirk in creed; prostrating to or calling upon other than Allah is shirk in action.

shirk-advanced-3.question: How does the shirk of the polytheists of Makkah primarily manifest according to the Quran?
options: They largely affirmed Allah as Creator but directed worship (dua, sacrifice, etc.) to others as intermediaries
shirk-advanced-3.explanation: The Quran shows that the mushrikin acknowledged Allah as Creator and Sustainer but said they worshipped others only to bring them closer to Allah.

shirk-advanced-4.question: What is the ruling on the one who makes intermediaries between himself and Allah, calling upon them and putting trust in them?
options: He is a sinner but Muslim
He is a disbeliever by scholarly consensus
It is recommended for the common people
shirk-advanced-4.explanation: One of the nullifiers of Islam is to set up intermediaries between oneself and Allah, calling upon them, asking them, and putting trust in them.

shirk-advanced-5.question: What is the correct understanding of the verse 'They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah'?
options: It only refers to literal worship
It includes obeying them in making lawful what Allah made unlawful and unlawful what Allah made lawful
shirk-advanced-5.explanation: When Adi ibn Hatim heard this verse, the Prophet ﷺ explained that it meant taking as lawful what they made lawful and unlawful what they made unlawful.

shirk-advanced-6.question: What is the difference between the general and specific Ma'iyyah of Allah, and how does misunderstanding it lead to shirk?
options: General Ma'iyyah is with all creation by knowledge and power; specific is with the believers by support. Believing Allah is mixed with creation is a form of shirk or deviation
Allah is only with the believers
shirk-advanced-6.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm Allah's withness without mixing or incarnation. Pantheistic or incarnationist beliefs fall into shirk or major deviation.

shirk-advanced-7.question: What is the ruling on the one who believes that the Quran is created?
options: It is a major innovation that opposes the creed of Ahlus-Sunnah; the Quran is the uncreated Speech of Allah
It is only a linguistic issue
shirk-advanced-7.explanation: The view that the Quran is created was a major fitnah. Ahlus-Sunnah affirm that the Quran is the eternal, uncreated Kalam of Allah.

shirk-advanced-8.question: How can minor shirk become major shirk?
options: When the person holds a belief that elevates the object to the level of a rival to Allah (e.g., believing the one sworn by has the same status as Allah)
shirk-advanced-8.explanation: Minor shirk remains minor as long as the heart does not equate the object with Allah. When the belief reaches the level of taking a rival, it becomes major.

shirk-advanced-9.question: What is the correct position on seeking blessing from the graves of the righteous?
options: It is forbidden and a means that led previous nations into shirk; the Prophet ﷺ severely warned against it
It is permissible if done with pure intention
shirk-advanced-9.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ forbade taking graves as places of worship and warned that excessive veneration of the righteous leads to shirk.

shirk-advanced-10.question: What is the ruling on the one who mocks Allah, His Messenger, or the religion of Islam?
options: He is a sinner but remains Muslim
He has committed major kufr and left Islam, whether done seriously or in jest
It is only minor if in jest
shirk-advanced-10.explanation: Allah says about those who mocked: 'Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.'

shirk-advanced-11.question: What is the precise danger of the statement 'Had it not been for so-and-so, such-and-such would not have happened' when said with attachment of the heart?
options: It can be minor shirk in speech and, if the heart relies on the person as the true cause, it approaches major shirk
It is only a linguistic error
shirk-advanced-11.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught to say 'What Allah willed, then what so-and-so willed.' Relying on created beings as independent causes is a form of shirk.

shirk-advanced-12.question: What is the ruling on the one who believes that some of the awliya have the ability to dispose of the affairs of the universe (tasarruf)?
options: It is a high spiritual station
It is major shirk because disposal of the universe belongs only to Allah
It is acceptable in some Sufi paths
shirk-advanced-12.explanation: Believing that any created being has independent control or disposal over the universe is major shirk in Rububiyyah.

shirk-advanced-13.question: What is the correct understanding of the hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ said that shirk is more hidden than the crawling of an ant?
options: Even believers can fall into subtle forms of shirk (especially riya and attachment of the heart) without realizing, so constant vigilance and dua are required
shirk-advanced-13.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught a specific dua seeking refuge from associating partners with Allah knowingly and asking forgiveness for what one does unknowingly.

shirk-advanced-14.question: What is the ruling on the one who does not declare the polytheists to be disbelievers, or doubts their disbelief?
options: He is still a full Muslim
He himself is a disbeliever according to the consensus of the scholars
It is a minor difference of opinion
It is only a political matter
shirk-advanced-14.explanation: One of the clear nullifiers of Islam is failing to regard the mushrikin as kuffar, or doubting their disbelief, or approving of their religion.

shirk-advanced-15.question: What is the difference between the shirk of the Christians and the shirk of the Arab polytheists according to the scholars?
options: The Arab polytheists mainly committed shirk in Uluhiyyah while affirming Rububiyyah; the Christians committed shirk in both Rububiyyah (Trinity) and Uluhiyyah
shirk-advanced-15.explanation: The Christians' belief in the Trinity is shirk in Rububiyyah and Asma wa Sifat, while also involving shirk in worship.

shirk-advanced-16.question: What is the ruling on the one who believes that the dead can hear and respond to calls for help in the same way as the living?
options: It is a false belief that leads to major shirk when one calls upon them for help
It is established by the Quran
shirk-advanced-16.explanation: The Quran states that the dead do not hear in the sense of responding to calls for help. Calling upon them is major shirk.

shirk-advanced-17.question: What is the correct position on the issue of whether minor shirk is forgiven without repentance?
options: Like other sins, it requires repentance; Allah may forgive it or hold the person accountable
It is only a cultural issue
shirk-advanced-17.explanation: Minor shirk is still a serious sin. One must repent from it. Allah may forgive it by His mercy or punish for it, but it does not expel from Islam.

shirk-advanced-18.question: What is the ruling on the one who supports or allies with the disbelievers against the Muslims out of love for their religion?
options: If done out of love for their religion or approval of their disbelief, it is a nullifier of Islam
It is only a minor sin
shirk-advanced-18.explanation: Taking the disbelievers as allies in preference to the believers, especially with approval of their religion, is a form of disbelief mentioned in the Quran.

shirk-advanced-19.question: What is the precise meaning of the condition of 'rejection of taghut' in the Shahadah?
options: Disbelieving in and rejecting everything that is worshipped besides Allah, and declaring it false
shirk-advanced-19.explanation: The Shahadah requires both affirmation of Allah's sole right to worship and rejection (kufr) of all taghut — everything worshipped besides Him.

shirk-advanced-20.question: What is the ruling on the one who believes that some people are not required to follow the Shariah of Muhammad ﷺ?
options: It is a valid spiritual station
It is major disbelief because the Shariah of Muhammad ﷺ is for all of humanity until the Day of Judgment
It is only a difference of schools
shirk-advanced-20.explanation: Believing that anyone is exempt from the final Shariah, or that another path is better, is a nullifier of Islam.

shirk-advanced-21.question: How does the concept of 'blocking the means' (sadd adh-dhara'i) apply to minor shirk?
options: Many forms of minor shirk are prohibited to block the path to major shirk
shirk-advanced-21.explanation: The Shariah prohibits means that lead to major shirk, such as certain forms of oaths, amulets, and excessive veneration of the righteous.

shirk-advanced-22.question: What is the correct belief about the hearing of the dead in the context of avoiding shirk?
options: The dead hear everything and can respond
The dead may hear in a limited sense (as in the hadith of the well of Badr), but they cannot respond to calls for help; calling upon them is still shirk
The dead hear nothing at all
shirk-advanced-22.explanation: Even if limited hearing is affirmed, the dead cannot fulfill requests or help. Calling upon them remains major shirk.

shirk-advanced-23.question: What is the ruling on the one who claims that the awliya know the unseen or have independent knowledge of future events?
options: It is a false claim and a form of shirk in Asma wa Sifat, because knowledge of the unseen belongs only to Allah
It is established for the highest ranks
shirk-advanced-23.explanation: Allah alone knows the unseen. Any claim that created beings possess independent knowledge of the ghayb is a form of shirk.

shirk-advanced-24.question: What is the correct understanding of the verse 'Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him'?
options: It is a command that establishes the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped, making any worship of others major shirk
It applies only to the Prophets
shirk-advanced-24.explanation: This verse and similar ones form the foundation of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah; violating it by directing worship to others is major shirk.

shirk-advanced-25.question: What is the ruling on the one who turns away from the judgment of Allah and seeks judgment from taghut while believing the taghut judgment is better?
options: He is a sinner but Muslim
It is only minor if temporary
shirk-advanced-25.explanation: Preferring the judgment of taghut over the judgment of Allah, or believing it is better, is clear kufr according to the Quran and the nullifiers of Islam.

shirk-advanced-26.question: What is the precise reason why riya is called minor shirk?
options: Because the person still directs the outward act toward Allah, but shares the intention with the desire for praise from people
Because it is only in the heart
shirk-advanced-26.explanation: In riya, the act of worship is performed, but the intention is contaminated by seeking the praise of creation. This is minor shirk that nullifies or diminishes the reward.

shirk-advanced-27.question: What is the ruling on the one who believes that the Prophet ﷺ has the right of independent intercession without Allah's permission?
options: It is a high level of respect
It is a form of shirk because all intercession belongs to Allah and occurs only by His permission
shirk-advanced-27.explanation: The Quran affirms that intercession is entirely in Allah's hands. No one intercedes except after His permission.

shirk-advanced-28.question: What is the correct methodology for protecting oneself from both major and minor shirk?
options: Learn pure Tawhid from the Quran and Sunnah, constantly renew sincerity, make the dua of seeking refuge from shirk, and avoid all means that lead to shirk
shirk-advanced-28.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught a specific dua: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating partners with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do unknowingly.'

shirk-advanced-29.question: What is the ruling on the one who claims that some verses of the Quran or some hadiths are not applicable today because of modern times?
options: If it involves rejecting clear obligations or making lawful what Allah made unlawful, it can reach the level of disbelief
It is only a difference of interpretation
shirk-advanced-29.explanation: Rejecting clear texts of the Quran or Sunnah, or claiming they are no longer applicable, can constitute major disbelief depending on the nature of the rejection.

shirk-advanced-30.question: What is the final outcome for the one who dies upon pure Tawhid, free of major shirk, even if he had major sins?
options: He will eventually enter Paradise by Allah's mercy, after possible purification if Allah wills
He is equal to the Prophets
His sins are automatically erased without any process
shirk-advanced-30.explanation: The one who dies upon Tawhid will enter Paradise. Major sinners among the believers may be punished for a time if Allah wills, then enter Paradise by His mercy and the intercession He grants.

shirk-advanced-31.question: What is the comprehensive way to understand the relationship between shirk and the nullifiers of Islam?
options: Major shirk is the first and most serious of the nullifiers; other nullifiers are forms of kufr that may or may not involve shirk
Shirk is separate from the nullifiers
shirk-advanced-31.explanation: The ten nullifiers begin with shirk. Other nullifiers include setting up intermediaries, not declaring mushrikin as disbelievers, preferring other laws, mocking the religion, and supporting disbelievers against Muslims out of love for their religion.

shirk-advanced-32.question: What is the ultimate protection from falling into shirk according to the Quran and Sunnah?
options: Relying on one's own knowledge alone
Sincere attachment to pure Tawhid, constant dua for steadfastness, learning the boundaries of Tawhid and shirk, and following the way of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions
Avoiding all forms of worship that involve other people
shirk-advanced-32.explanation: The Quran and Sunnah emphasize knowledge of Tawhid, sincerity, seeking refuge from shirk, and adhering to the path of the Salaf as the protection from all forms of associating partners with Allah.

shirk-advanced-33.question: What is the ruling on the one who believes that the angels or jinn have independent authority to decree benefit or harm?
options: It is a high level of faith in the unseen
It is major shirk because decree and control belong only to Allah
It is acceptable in some traditions
shirk-advanced-33.explanation: Angels and jinn are created servants of Allah. Attributing independent authority of decree, benefit, or harm to them is major shirk in Rububiyyah.

shirk-advanced-34.question: What is the correct understanding of the statement that 'shirk is the greatest form of oppression (zulm)'?
options: It is only a moral statement
It is the greatest injustice because it denies Allah His exclusive right to be worshipped and ascribes His rights to others
It applies only to major sins of the limbs
shirk-advanced-34.explanation: Luqman called shirk a great injustice. It is the greatest oppression because it violates the most fundamental right of the Creator.

shirk-advanced-35.question: What is the ruling on the one who claims that certain acts of worship (such as tawaf or sacrifice) can be directed to other than Allah for the sake of nearness?
options: It is a valid means of nearness
It is major shirk because all acts of worship must be directed purely to Allah alone
It is permissible if the intention is good
shirk-advanced-35.explanation: Any act of worship — including tawaf, sacrifice, vow, or dua — directed to other than Allah is major shirk, regardless of the claim of seeking nearness.

shirk-advanced-36.question: What is the comprehensive definition of shirk that covers both major and minor forms according to the texts?
options: Ascribing a partner or rival to Allah in any of His exclusive rights — whether in Lordship, worship, or Names and Attributes — whether that reaches the level of expelling from Islam or remains a serious sin that diminishes Tawhid
Only the actions of the polytheists of the past
shirk-advanced-36.explanation: This definition encompasses major shirk (which expels from Islam) and minor shirk (which does not, but is still a grave sin that compromises pure Tawhid).
